Committee: Ways and Means General Fund
Sponsor: Orr
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 02/24/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 112 as substituted and reported by the Committee on Ways and Means General Fund would reduce the current additional license tax and registration fee of either $200 or $100, established for battery or plug-in hybrid electric vehicles, respectively, pursuant to the Rebuild Alabama Act, to $50 for electric low speed vehicles (LSV) that are registered and operated on the public (non-interstate) highways of this state. Based on the number of LSV's registered in fiscal year 2020, beginning January 1, 2022, this bill would reduce LSV license tax and registration fee receipts to the following funds by the following estimated amounts:
Public Road and Bridge Fund
$20,000
Counties and Municipalities
$10,000
Rebuild Alabama Fund
$10,000
Total
$40,000
Additionally, this bill establishes that the Alabama Department of Revenue is responsible for the distribution of the additional annual license and registration fees for electric vehicles beginning October 1, 2021, which will increase the administrative obligations of the department by an undetermined amount.
Kyle South, Vice Chair
Ways and Means General Fund

Committee: Governmental Affairs
Sponsor: Orr
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 02/09/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 112 as introduced would reduce the additional license tax and registration fee of $200, previously established for battery electric vehicles pursuant to the Rebuild Alabama Act, to $50 for electric low speed vehicles (LSV) that are registered and operated on the public (non-interstate) highways of this state.  Based on the number of LSV's registered in FY 2020, beginning January 1, 2022 this could reduce collections from LSV's by an estimated $40,200 per year, as follows:
Public Road and Bridge Fund
$20,000
Counties and Municipalities
$10,000
Rebuild Alabama Fund
$10,000
Jimmy Holley, Chairperson
Governmental Affairs

Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Security
Sponsor: Sorrell
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 04/26/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 405 as introduced revises certain restrictions regarding the carrying or possession of a pistol.
This bill could decrease potential receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general funds from fines; decrease potential receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could decrease potential obligations of the district attorneys and local jails by an undetermined amount dependent on the number of persons would have otherwise been charged with and convicted of violating provisions regarding carrying a concealed pistol and the penalties that would have been imposed.
Allen Treadaway, Chair
Public Safety and Homeland Security

Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Security
Sponsor: Sorrell
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 04/27/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 405 as substituted and reported by the Committee on Public Safety and Homeland Security revises certain restrictions regarding the carrying or possession of a pistol, and eliminates the requirement to obtain a pistol permit in order to carry a concealed pistol.
Additionally, this bill could reduce receipts to the several counties, by an undetermined amount, dependent on the number of individuals that would no longer obtain a concealed carry permit to carry a concealed pistol and the cost of the permit.
This bill could decrease potential receipts to the State General Fund and municipal general funds from fines; decrease potential receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds, municipal general funds, and other funds to which court costs are deposited; and could decrease potential obligations of the district attorneys and local jails by an undetermined amount dependent on the number of persons would have otherwise been charged with and convicted of violating provisions regarding carrying a concealed pistol and the penalties that would have been imposed.
Allen Treadaway, Chair
Public Safety and Homeland Security

Committee: State Government
Sponsor: Wood (R)
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 03/08/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House bill 163 as introduced would increase receipts to the Alabama Department of Revenue by an estimated $77,000 annually for processing electronic title payments for motor vehicles or manufactured homes and collecting and retaining the commission fee of $1.50, based on Fiscal Year 2020 data. The bill provides that any commission fees collected would be continuously appropriated to the department.
Chris Pringle, Chair
State Government
